---
title: "GLMMTMB Analysis for PSD-95 Methylation Data (filtered)"
---

```{r}
# ==============================================================
# switch to glmmtmb for more flexible modeling
# ==============================================================
# glmmTMB advantages for your methylation data:
# - Direct Beta family on raw proportions (0-1) → no need for M-values
# - Better convergence on complex structures
# - Handles zero/one-inflation if present (common in methylation)
# - Similar syntax to lme4

# Install if needed (once): install.packages("glmmTMB")
library(glmmTMB)
library(DHARMa)      # For better residuals diagnostics
library(performance) # For R2, ICC, etc.
library(emmeans)     # Post-hoc (works with glmmTMB)
```


```{r}
# ==============================================================
# Load Data (as in your code - assuming already run)
 psd95 <- suppressWarnings(read_xlsx("~/Work/TBM-R-Analysis/tables/Rohdaten/PSD95_CpGs_mit_verhalten_größer_umstrukturiert.xlsx"))
# ==============================================================
```


```{r}
# ==============================================================
# 1. Filter to Specific CpGs of Interest
# ==============================================================
# Assuming "filter for" means keep only these CpGs (e.g., for focused analysis)
# If you meant exclude them, change to !CpG_Position %in% ...
psd95_specific <- psd95 %>%
  filter(CpG_Position %in% c("p95", "p60", "p23"))
```


```{r}
# ==============================================================
# 2. Preprocessing: Identify and Exclude Invariant/Low-Variability CpGs (among the specific ones)
# ==============================================================

# Compute summary stats per CpG across ALL samples
cpg_summary <- psd95_specific %>%
  group_by(CpG_Position) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_meth = mean(methylation, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_meth = sd(methylation, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_meth = min(methylation, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_meth = max(methylation, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n()
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    range_meth = max_meth - min_meth,
    is_invariant = (sd_meth == 0 | range_meth < 0.05)  # Threshold: SD=0 or range<5%
  )

# Print to inspect
print(cpg_summary)

# Filter data to exclude invariant CpGs (if any among the 3)
psd95_filtered <- psd95_specific %>%
  inner_join(cpg_summary %>% filter(!is_invariant) %>% select(CpG_Position), by = "CpG_Position")
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================
# Prepare Raw Proportion (Ensure Strictly (0,1) for Beta Family)
# ==============================================================
# Beta family requires 0 < y < 1. If any exact 0 or 1, add small epsilon or use zero_one_inflated_beta
psd95_beta <- psd95_filtered %>%
  mutate(
    meth_prop = methylation,  # Assume already 0-1 proportion
    # Adjust extremes if needed (common safe practice)
    meth_prop_adj = case_when(
      meth_prop == 0 ~ 0.0001,
      meth_prop == 1 ~ 0.9999,
      TRUE ~ meth_prop
    )
  )

# Check for exact 0/1
table(psd95_beta$meth_prop == 0 | psd95_beta$meth_prop == 1)
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================
# 1. Beta Model (Recommended: Proper Distribution for Proportions)
# ==============================================================
model_beta <- glmmTMB(
  meth_prop_adj ~ Gruppe * Zeitpunkt + Age_start + Sex +
                  (1 | ID:CpG_Position),   # Nested random intercept (your best structure)
  data = psd95_beta,
  family = beta_family(link = "logit")     # Logit link for proportions
)

# Summary
summary(model_beta)

# Performance metrics (R2 equivalent for GLMM)
r2(model_beta)           # Nakagawa R2 (marginal/conditional)
icc(model_beta)          # Intraclass correlation

# Residual diagnostics (better than base plot)
sim_resid <- simulateResiduals(model_beta)
plot(sim_resid)          # Check for normality, heteroscedasticity, zero-inflation
testDispersion(sim_resid)
testZeroInflation(sim_resid)
```
```{r}
library(report)
report(model_beta)
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================
# 2. Post-Hoc on Response Scale (Methylation Proportion)
# ==============================================================
# Marginal means and contrasts on original proportion scale
emm_beta <- emmeans(model_beta, ~ Gruppe | Zeitpunkt, type = "response")
emm_beta                     # Means (proportions)
pairs(emm_beta)              # Group differences per time

emm_time <- emmeans(model_beta, ~ Zeitpunkt | Gruppe, type = "response")
pairs(emm_time, adjust = "tukey")

# Interaction plot
emmip(model_beta, Gruppe ~ Zeitpunkt, CIs = TRUE, type = "response") +
  labs(y = "Predicted Methylation Proportion", title = "PSD-95 Promoter (Beta Model)")
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================
# 3. Alternative: Zero-One-Inflated Beta (If Diagnostics Show Excess 0/1)
# ==============================================================
# If testZeroInflation() significant or many extremes
model_zoi <- glmmTMB(
  meth_prop ~ Gruppe * Zeitpunkt + Age_start + Sex +
              (1 | ID:CpG_Position),
  ziformula = ~ Gruppe * Zeitpunkt,   # Predictors for zero/one inflation
  data = psd95_beta,
  family = beta_family(link = "logit")
  # Or use ziGamma if needed, but beta is best
)

summary(model_zoi)
plot(simulateResiduals(model_zoi))
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================
# 4. Gaussian on M-Values (For Direct Comparison to Your lmer)
# ==============================================================
model_gaussian_tmb <- glmmTMB(
  M_value ~ Gruppe * Zeitpunkt + Age_start + Sex +
            (1 | ID:CpG_Position),
  data = psd95_filtered,
  family = gaussian()
)

summary(model_gaussian_tmb)
r2(model_gaussian_tmb)   # Should match your lmer closely
```
